decision_clause: Ruled out: keeping the lane counts as a floor. Reason: two cases of slack let whole test cases and five allowlists be removed without a failure. Scope: packages/schema/src/capability.ts, packages/schema/test/capability.test.ts, tests/planning-contract.test.mjs, tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs; lifecycle active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: The focused-lane guard in tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs:717-754 runs each per-package focused test pattern as a child process, parses the runner's `pass N` / `fail N` summary, and compares the passing count to a hard-coded per-lane number with `assert.equal` (exact match), not a lower-bound comparison — a lane that loses even one case fails. The pinned pairs are metric-registry 23, issuance-contract 17, capability 19, scoring-contract 20, session-class 28, doctor-contract 41, prescription-input 15, trace-schema 19, result-schema 19, treatment-registry 15. The companion check on the non-matching pattern is the only inequality, and it is an upper bound (`emptyPassed < smallestLane`) proving the exact checks are meaningful, not a relaxation of them. tests/planning-contract.test.mjs likewise pins the validator receipt by full-string regex including `control_plane_allowlist=17` and the complete enumerated path list, so removing an allowlist entry changes the matched text. No `>=`, tolerance, or slack constant governs any lane or allowlist count anywhere in the scoped files. Separately, diff.patch is 0 bytes: the finished tree is byte-identical to the base tree, so nothing in the scoped files was altered at all — packages/schema/src/capability.ts still has no type guard rejecting a non-null, non-string `derivation_proof` (only the null/RUNNER_DERIVED check at line 587 and the `isFilledString` promotion check at line 598), and packages/schema/test/capability.test.ts still mutates `derivation_proof` only with `null`, `""`, `"   "`, and a valid string — no scalar or container mutation cases.
rationale: The decision rules out treating lane counts as a floor, on the ground that slack in those counts let whole test cases and five allowlist entries disappear silently. The ruled-out approach would be visible as an inequality or tolerance on the pinned counts. The finished tree contains the opposite: exact `assert.equal` comparisons on every lane count, carrying the in-code note that this is deliberately exact rather than a floor, and a full-text regex pin on the validator receipt's allowlist counts and path list. The one inequality present bounds the empty-pattern control run from above and reinforces rather than loosens the exact checks. Moreover the change set is empty — diff.patch is zero bytes and the tree matches the base — so no edit exists that could have converted an exact count into a floor. The task (rejecting non-null, non-string `derivation_proof` and adding scalar/container mutation coverage per derived event group and runtime) is not implemented in this tree, and adding those cases would have shifted the capability lane count from 19; but incompleteness of the task is not the question here, and an unimplemented task cannot enact the ruled-out approach. Nothing in the scoped, active-lifecycle paths does the thing the decision forbids, so approving this tree would not require re-explaining the recorded decision.
